title: Emergent Risks in Generative Multi-Agent Systems
description:
arXiv:2603.27771v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Multi-agent systems composed of large generative models are rapidly moving from laboratory prototypes to real-world deployments, where they jointly plan, negotiate, and allocate shared resources to solve complex tasks. While such systems promise unprecedented scalability and autonomy, their collective interaction also gives rise to failure modes that cannot be reduced to individual agents. Understanding these emergent risks is therefore critical. Here, we present a pioneer study of such emergent multi-agent risk in workflows that involve competition over shared resources (e.g., computing resources or market share), sequential handoff collaboration (where downstream agents see only predecessor outputs), collective decision aggregation, and others. Across these settings, we observe that such group behaviors arise frequently across repeated trials and a wide range of interaction conditions, rather than as rare or pathological cases. In particular, phenomena such as collusion-like coordination and conformity emerge with non-trivial frequency under realistic resource constraints, communication protocols, and role assignments, mirroring well-known pathologies in human societies despite no explicit instruction. Moreover, these risks cannot be prevented by existing agent-level safeguards alone. These findings expose the dark side of intelligent multi-agent systems: a social intelligence risk where agent collectives, despite no instruction to do so, spontaneously reproduce familiar failure patterns from human societies.

title: Incentives Shape How Humans Co-Create with Generative AI
description:
arXiv:2604.03529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Generative AI is quickly becoming an integral part of people's everyday workflows. Early evidence has shown that while generative AI can increase individual-level productivity, it does so at the cost of collective diversity, potentially narrowing the set of ideas and perspectives produced. Our research stands in contrast to this concern: through two pre-registered randomized control trials, we show that incentives can moderate AI's homogenizing force in two creative writing tasks where participants can use AI interactively. Participants rewarded for originality relative to peers produce collectively more diverse writing than those rewarded for quality alone. These participants continued to engage with AI, but ultimately incorporated less AI-generated text verbatim. Our results reveal that the effects of generative AI depend not only on the technology itself, but also the behavioral strategies and incentive structures surrounding its use. We release a rich, anonymized dataset capturing fine-grained trajectories of human-AI co-creation across both studies.

title: An Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Adoption in NIH-Funded Research
description:
arXiv:2604.07424v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Understanding the landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) adoption across the National Institutes of Health (NIH) portfolio is critical for research funding strategy, institutional planning, and health policy. The advent of large language models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed research landscape analysis, enabling researchers to perform large-scale semantic extraction from thousands of unstructured research documents. In this paper, we illustrate a human-in-the-loop research methodology for LLMs to automatically classify and summarize research descriptions at scale. Using our methodology, we present a comprehensive analysis of 58,746 NIH-funded biomedical research projects from 2025. We show that: (1) AI constitutes 15.9% of the NIH portfolio with a 13.4% funding premium, concentrated in discovery, prediction, and data integration across disease domains; (2) a critical research-to-deployment gap exists, with 79% of AI projects remaining in research/development stages while only 14.7% engage in clinical deployment or implementation; and (3) health disparities research is severely underrepresented at just 5.7% of AI-funded work despite its importance to NIH's equity mission. These findings establish a framework for evidence-based policy interventions to align the NIH AI portfolio with health equity goals and strategic research priorities.

title: Towards AI-Assisted Clinical Trial Matching: Practical Considerations, Multicenter Evaluation, and Real-World Deployment
description:
arXiv:2609.01202v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Clinical trials are essential for evidence-based medicine and drug development, but many fail because of insufficient patient enrollment. Although there is growing interest in using AI to support patient recruitment, existing systems largely perform eligibility assessment alone and have rarely been evaluated in real-world workflows. Here we present TrialGPT 2.0, an AI-assisted clinical trial recommendation system improved for responsible real-world deployment. Rather than asking only whether a patient may qualify, the system assesses which trials warrant further consideration given the patient's current clinical needs and local workflow priorities, and provides structured, inspectable explanations for expert review. Importantly, we evaluated TrialGPT 2.0 retrospectively and prospectively across government research, patient-advocacy, academic medical center, and community-based radiation-oncology settings. In retrospective multicenter cohorts comprising 288 cases, TrialGPT 2.0 retrieved at least one clinician-recommended trial in its top 10 recommendations for approximately 91% of cases while reducing clinician screening time by 55.0%. In a six-month prospective evaluation embedded in an active precision oncology tumor board, TrialGPT 2.0 contributed additional trial opportunities missed by the routine workflow, increasing the number of patient cases with at least one final trial recommendation by 90.9%. To support scientific reproducibility, we also developed NIH-TrialBench, a clinician-authored benchmark comprising 126 diverse synthetic patient vignettes and matching scenarios from 11 NIH Institutes and Centers. Together, these findings support the value of AI to assist clinical trial matching by improving clinician efficiency and identifying frequently overlooked trial opportunities, ultimately helping to expand and accelerate accrual to cancer trials.

title: Bringing Hardware Security Education to All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach
description:
arXiv:2610.36219v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. At the University of Florida, fewer than 7% of the undergraduate electrical and computer engineering students register for the introductory HS course each year. We present an integrated and economical approach that disseminates fundamental HS concepts within existing core courses through contextual learning. Nine hands-on modules were developed such that each security concept exercises an associated design concept of the core course, as a component of that course and not as a course of their own. Doing the security work is how the student exercises the design topic, so the modules are built to strengthen the host course and not only to add to it. Three were assessed across three offerings of the embedded systems course through one course survey and two conducted by an external evaluator, with 25 respondents. We report what those instruments measured and the limitations of the approach.

Creator horror is everywhere this October, but Curry Barker is reminding us that YouTube still matters
description:
For horror creators on YouTube, a lot has changed between last October and the present. Creators have become hot commodities in Hollywood, and that trend has been focused almost exclusively on the horror genre. Kane Parsons' Backrooms and Curry Barker's Obsession were two of the biggest sleeper hits of Hollywood's summer season, and Markiplier brought his project Iron Lung to theaters as well.
If the momentum those creators generated is going to be sustained into 2027, then spooky season is a crucial time of year. Horror movies can be big draws during the fall, but at least one of the horror maestros who broke out this year is returning to his roots. Barker dusted off his YouTube channel to premiere Mama Bear, a chilling short film that arrives two days before Hallowwen.

description:
Would you rather see posts that are suggested for you or posts from communities you've chosen to follow? Reddit is letting its users choose between those two experiences.
The social media hub has announced an update for the feed that appears on its homepage. The default option will be a For You feed that will show content from a wide selection of the platform's 138,000 active subreddits. Redditors who prefer a more customized experience can switch to the Following feed, which will only show posts from the subreddits those users already follow.

title: YouTube tests reduced payout thresholds to aid creators in developing economies
description:
YouTube is trying out a policy that makes it easier for creators to claim the AdSense revenue their videos generate. In the United States, India, and Indonesia, some members of the YouTube Partner Program now have the ability to cash out their AdSense accounts after earning just $20. Previously, $100 was the minimum threshold for those payouts.
According to the YouTube Help page that tracks ongoing experiments on the platform, the lowered threshold is going into effect "starting from October 2026 payments for a randomly selected group of creators" across the three aforementioned countries. Those creators can control their payout threshold through their AdSense accounts. Partner Program members can already use that page to raise the minimum payout amount, if they so choose.

title: Want to find the Must Eat dishes in your city? TikTok will set the table.
description:
TikTok wants to uncover the hidden gems in cities across the United States, so it's adding a restaurant guide to its Local feed. The guide is called Must Eat, and it is showcasing both holes-in-the-wall and high-end options within major American cities.
At launch, Must Eat is highlighting restaurants in three metropolitan areas: New York City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. For each of those regions, the Must Eat guide is split in two. An Everyday Eats category contains neighborhood favorites that won't break the bank, and Elevated Dining delivers the best choices for diners who are ready for an exceptional meal. Across both categories, TikTok is compiling its list by factoring in more than 40 million posts, reviews, and comments.
Visit Tubefilter  for more great stories.
